st.2: Rakhigarhi is not yet a World Heritage Site; it is on UNESCO's Tentative List.

x: All three statements are correct: Dholavira was inscribed in 2021 as India's 40th site, Rakhigarhi is only on the Tentative List, and Mohenjodaro has been a World Heritage Site since 1980.

st.3: Specialised shell work was concentrated at Nageshwar and Balakot.

x: All three statements are correct: Chanhudaro is the 'Lancashire of India' and Lothal the 'Manchester' of the Harappans, Chanhudaro was a bead-making craft town, and specialised shell work came from Nageshwar and Balakot.

st.2: Lost-wax casting began in India only with the Chola bronzes such as the Nataraja.
st.1: Kalibangan has yielded a gold foundry with an active furnace.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the gold foundry with an active furnace is from Rakhigarhi, not Kalibangan. Statement 2 is incorrect: lost-wax casting goes back to the Harappans (Dancing Girl) and continued in the Daimabad bronzes long before the Chola Nataraja.

st.2: It records that the Sudarshana lake was first built by Pushyagupta under Chandragupta Maurya.

x: All three statements are correct: it is the first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit, it says the Sudarshana lake was built by Pushyagupta under Chandragupta Maurya (Tushaspha added conduits under Ashoka), and the same rock carries Ashoka's fourteen major rock edicts.

st.2: The earliest land-grant records in India are those of the Satavahanas.

x: All three statements are correct: inscriptions are the most reliable source, the earliest land grants are Satavahana records, and stratigraphy rests on superposition (a lower layer is older).

st.1: Women were not allowed to own cattle.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: widow remarriage was possible. Statement 1 is incorrect: Rig Vedic women could own cattle. Statement 2 is incorrect: child marriage was not common in the Rig Vedic period.

st.3: Adichanallur in Thoothukudi district is an Iron Age urn-burial site of the far south.

x: All three statements are correct: Sivagalai iron is dated to about 2953 BCE, Mayiladumparai iron to 2172 BCE, and Adichanallur (Thoothukudi) is a southern Iron Age urn-burial site, not a Painted Grey Ware site.

st.3: An arama, such as Nandaluru, is a single rock-cut prayer hall without any stupa or vihara.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: a chaitya is a prayer hall with a stupa at its apsidal end. Statement 2 is incorrect: a vihara is a monastery; the solid relic mound is a stupa. Statement 3 is incorrect: an arama such as Nandaluru is a complex of stupa, vihara, chaitya and school.

st.3: Ashoka's Thirteenth Rock Edict names the Ajivikas along with the Brahmanas, the Sangha and the Nirgranthas.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Ajivikas were popular under Bindusara. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Barabar caves were gifted to the Ajivikas by Ashoka (and Nagarjuni caves by Dasharatha), not Chandragupta Maurya. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is the Seventh Pillar Edict that names the Ajivikas with the Brahmanas, the Sangha and the Nirgranthas.

st.3: The Digambaras do not accept the Svetambara canon and hold that the original Angas were lost.

x: All three statements are correct: the Ganadharas compiled the 12 Angas, the Acharanga Sutra gives the monks' code and the Bhagavati Sutra the doctrines, and the Digambaras reject the Svetambara canon, holding the original Angas lost.

st.1: One verse of the Arthashastra names its author Bhadrabahu.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: in the Mudrarakshasa, Rakshasa is the Nanda minister. Statement 1 is incorrect: the verse names the author Vishnugupta, not Bhadrabahu. Statement 2 is incorrect: Taranath and Jain tradition keep him on as Bindusara's minister, not Ashoka's.

st.1: It was a new religion, not merely a moral code and social ethic.
st.2: Its central point was peace and non-violence; Rock Edict XIII bans slaughter and sacrifice.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Pillar Edict II defines Dhamma as 'few faults, many good deeds'. Statement 1 is incorrect: Dhamma was a moral code and social ethic, not a new religion. Statement 2 is incorrect: the ban on slaughter and sacrifice is in Rock Edict I (Rock Edict XIII records Kalinga). Statement 4 is incorrect: Dhamma does not name the Four Noble Truths or Nibbana.

st.3: The Astynomoi were in charge of roads, irrigation and land measurement.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Pataliputra was run by a board of 30 in six committees of five. Statement 2 is incorrect: the sixth committee collected the tax on sales, not land revenue. Statement 3 is incorrect: roads, irrigation and land measurement were under the Agronomoi (district officers); the Astynomoi were city officers.

st.1: Brihadratha, the last Maurya, was the immediate successor of Ashoka.
st.2: The Sunga dynasty was founded around 232 BC.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Dhanadeva's Ayodhya inscription refers to Pushyamitra's two Ashvamedhas. Statement 1 is incorrect: Brihadratha was the seventh king after Ashoka, not his immediate successor. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Sungas were founded around 187 BC (232 BC is Ashoka's death). Statement 3 is incorrect: Pushyamitra was a Brahmana of the Bharadvaja gotra.

st.2: His influence never reached Simhala.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: Samudragupta's empire stretched well beyond Magadha and the middle Ganga valley (Allahabad pillar). Statement 2: his influence reached Simhala, whose king Meghavarna sent an embassy to him.

st.1: He was a Buddhist pilgrim who visited India during the reign of Harsha.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: Fa-Hien came during the reign of Chandragupta II; it was Hiuen Tsang who came under Harsha. Statement 2: Fa-Hien did not name the reigning king.

st.3: The Deobaranark inscription belongs to the Later Gupta Jivitagupta II.

x: All three statements are correct: the Asirgarh seal is of the Maukhari Sarvavarman, the Haraha inscription records Ishanavarman's victories, and the Deobaranark inscription is of the Later Gupta Jivitagupta II.

st.4: He was buried at Mehrauli near the Qutb Minar in Delhi.
st.1: He was bought as a slave by Iltutmish before entering Muhammad Ghori's service.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Aibak was Amir-i-Akhur (Master of Stables). Statement 1 is incorrect: he was sold to the Qazi of Nishapur; it was Aibak who later bought Iltutmish. Statement 3 is incorrect: his capital was Lahore. Statement 4 is incorrect: he was buried near Anarkali Bazaar in Lahore, not at Mehrauli.

st.1: Khizr Khan was one of the weak Tughlaq successors of Firoz after 1388.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Tughlaq period is 1320-1414. Statement 1 is incorrect: Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty; Abu Bakr was one of Firoz's weak successors. Statement 2 is incorrect: Timur invaded in 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq, after Firoz's death.

st.2: Madhura Vijayam, which describes the conquest of the Madurai Sultanate, was written by Gangadevi.

x: All three statements are correct: the Madurai Sultanate was set up in 1335, Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam on Kumara Kampana's conquest of it, and Malik Maqbul, once a Telugu Brahmin, became Firoz Shah's wazir.

st.2: Alauddin Khalji's token currency failed through forgery.
st.1: Iltutmish's copper tanka weighed 175 grains.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Sher Shah's revenue system was the model for Todar Mal's bandobast. Statement 1 is incorrect: Iltutmish's tanka was silver (175 grains); the jital was copper. Statement 2 is incorrect: the token currency that failed through forgery was Muhammad bin Tughlaq's. Statement 3 is incorrect: 48 jitals made one tanka.

st.1: Rag Vibodh was written by Somanatha.

x: All three statements are correct: Rag Vibodh is Somanatha's work, Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music, and Man Kautuhal is associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar.

st.2: Chand Bibi resisted the Mughal attack on Ahmednagar.

x: All three statements are correct: Gujarat was taken in 1572-73 from Muzaffar Shah III, Chand Bibi defended Ahmednagar against the Mughals, and Asirgarh in Khandesh (1601) was Akbar's last campaign.

st.3: Banda Bahadur was executed in 1716 during the reign of Farrukhsiyar.

x: All three statements are correct: Bahadur Shah I released Shahu and was called 'Shah-i-Bekhabar', Jahandar Shah 'Lampat' had Zulfiqar Khan as wazir, and Banda Bahadur was executed in 1716 under Farrukhsiyar.

st.1: He was crowned at the age of five in 1839, immediately after Ranjit Singh's death.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the First Anglo-Sikh War ended with the Treaty of Lahore (1846). Statement 1 is incorrect: Kharak Singh succeeded Ranjit Singh in 1839; Duleep Singh was crowned in 1843. Statement 2 is incorrect: in 1887 he sought the help of Tsar Alexander III, not Nicholas II.

st.1: The Khalsa was founded at Paonta Sahib, where the first five volunteers, the Panj Pyare, were baptised.
st.4: Before he was killed at Nanded in 1708, Guru Gobind Singh declared Banda Bahadur the eternal Guru.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Zafarnama is Guru Gobind Singh's Persian letter to Aurangzeb. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Khalsa was founded at Anandpur (1699). Statement 2 is incorrect: the Chali Mukte died at Muktsar (Khidrana), not Anandpur. Statement 4 is incorrect: he declared the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru; Banda Bahadur was his military successor.

st.3: The Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by Akbar, not by Shah Jahan.
st.2: The Char Minar of Hyderabad was built by Ibrahim Qutb Shah in 1591.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: Babur's Ram Bagh is at Agra. Statement 2: the Char Minar (1591) was built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. Statement 3: the Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.

st.2: The halo (nimbus) behind the emperor's head first appeared in Mughal painting under Jahangir.

x: All three statements are correct: the Tasvir Khana had more than 100 painters under Abdus Samad, the halo appeared under Jahangir, and painters moved to provincial and Rajput courts when Aurangzeb withdrew patronage.

st.2: About 12,000 of his sankirtanas survive on copper plates at Srisailam.
st.1: The YSR Kadapa district is named after him.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: it is the Annamayya district that is named after him (YSR Kadapa is named after Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy). Statement 2: the 12,000 copper-plate sankirtanas survive at Tirumala, not Srisailam.

st.1: He composed about 32,000 sankirtanas to Lord Rama of Bhadrachalam.
st.4: Arudra called him 'Andhra Bhoja'.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: about 12,000 sankirtanas survive on copper plates found at Tirumala in 1922. Statement 1 is incorrect: his 32,000 sankirtanas were to Lord Venkateswara of Tirumala (Bhadrachalam Rama is Ramadasu's). Statement 3 is incorrect: the plates were recovered and edited by Veturi Prabhakara Sastry. Statement 4 is incorrect: Arudra called him 'Incarnated Telugu'; 'Andhra Bhoja' is Krishnadevaraya.

st.4: Nizamuddin Auliya equated Alakh Niranjan with Khuda in Hindi verse.
st.2: The Sufi text Amritakund was translated from Persian into Sanskrit.
st.1: The Nathpanth is traced to Gorakhnath, and Matsyendranath was his disciple.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the Nathpanth is traced to Matsyendranath, with Gorakhnath as its great yogi. Statement 2: Amritakund was a Hath-yoga text translated into Arabic and Persian. Statement 3: breath control was adopted in all orders except the Naqshbandi. Statement 4: it was Hamiduddin Nagori who equated Alakh Niranjan with Khuda.

st.2: Kashiraj Pandit, the eyewitness historian of the battle, was an official of Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh.

x: All three statements are correct: the Marathas' expulsion of Timur Shah from Lahore (1758) was the immediate cause, Kashiraj Pandit served Shuja-ud-Daula, and Maratha power recovered under Madhav Rao I.

st.2: Nizampatnam (Petapoli) was the site of an early Dutch factory on the Andhra coast.

x: All three statements are correct: Pulicat was the Dutch Coromandel headquarters till 1690, Nizampatnam (Petapoli) had an early Dutch factory, and Fort Geldria was built at Pulicat.

st.1: Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry fired at his officers at Barrackpore on 10 May 1857.
st.2: Mangal Pandey was hanged at Meerut on 8 April 1857 and the 34th Bengal Native Infantry was disbanded.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: Mangal Pandey fired at his officers on 29 March 1857 (10 May is the Meerut outbreak). Statement 2: he was hanged at Barrackpore, not Meerut. Statement 3: the 85 sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were sentenced to ten years' imprisonment.

st.3: Anwaruddin marched against the French after they took Madras.

x: All three statements are correct: the seizure of French ships by Barnet was the immediate cause, Anwaruddin made himself Nawab of Arcot in 1744, and he marched against the French after they took Madras (and was beaten at Adyar).

st.1: It was fought on 23 June 1764 at Palashi on the Bhagirathi.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Clive's 3,000 beat Siraj-ud-daula's 50,000. Statement 1 is incorrect: Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 (1764 is Buxar). Statement 2 is incorrect: the battlefield lies in Nadia district, not Murshidabad.

st.2: He set up the District Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats in 1793.
st.4: He raised the tribute paid to Shah Alam to Rs 26 lakh.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: in 1772 Hastings ended Dual Government and moved the treasury to Calcutta. Statement 2 is incorrect: he set up the district adalats in 1772; 1793 is the Cornwallis Code. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Code of Gentoo Laws was translated by Nathaniel Halhed. Statement 4 is incorrect: Hastings stopped the Rs 26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam.

st.3: It required the Supreme Court to respect the religious and social customs of Indians.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1781 Act exempted the Governor-General-in-Council for official acts, excluded revenue matters, and told the Court to respect Indian customs (the Board of Control came with Pitt's India Act, 1784).

st.2: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and Clement Attlee.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the third member was A.V. Alexander; Attlee was the Prime Minister who sent the Mission. Statement 4 is incorrect: 'The Viceroy's Journal' is Lord Wavell's.

st.2: The cotton mills were mostly Indian-owned, while the jute mills of Bengal were mostly foreign-owned.

x: All three statements are correct: Davar founded the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company (1854), cotton mills were mostly Indian-owned and jute mills foreign-owned, and capital goods were only about a fourth of output at independence.

st.2: The 1866 split was mainly caused by Keshab's opposition to inter-caste marriage.
st.4: The Native Marriage Act of 1856 is also known as the Brahmo Marriage Act.
st.1: After the 1866 split, Keshab Chandra Sen's body came to be known as the Adi Brahmo Samaj.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the Adi Brahmo Samaj was Debendranath Tagore's body; Keshab led the Brahmo Samaj of India. Statement 2: the split came from Keshab's radicalism, including his support for inter-caste marriage. Statement 3: the Indian Reform Association was founded in 1870. Statement 4: the Native (Brahmo) Marriage Act is of 1872 (1856 is the Widow Remarriage Act).

st.2: Tripuraneni's song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' belongs to the Civil Disobedience Movement.

x: All three statements are correct: Tripuraneni attacked caste and priestly dominance in Sutapuranam and Sambuka Vadha, his 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' belongs to Civil Disobedience, and Gurajada's patron court was Vizianagaram under Ananda Gajapati.

st.3: His Savara grammar (manual) of 1931 was written in English.

x: All three statements are correct: Gidugu was born at Ponduru and taught at Parlakimidi, received the Kaisar-e-Hind in 1934, and wrote his Savara manual (1931) in English.

st.2: The Rakhmabai case was a suit for restitution of conjugal rights filed by Rakhmabai against her husband.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Malabari of the Indian Spectator wrote 'Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood' (1884). Statement 2 is incorrect: the restitution suit was filed by her husband Dadaji against Rakhmabai. Statement 3 is incorrect: Phulmoni Dasi's death pushed the Age of Consent Act (1891), not the Sarda Act.

st.1: The Darul Uloom at Deoband, in Saharanpur district, was founded in 1875 by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi.
st.3: In 1888 the Deoband leaders issued a fatwa in support of Sir Syed's United Patriotic Association.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Deoband school welcomed the Congress. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Darul Uloom was founded in 1866 (1875 is Sir Syed's Aligarh college). Statement 2 is incorrect: Mahmud-ul-Hasan's political turn led to the Jamiat-ul-Ulema-e-Hind in 1919, not 1906. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 1888 fatwa was against Sir Syed's United Patriotic Association.

st.2: It issued no hukamnamas and kept no worship places or priests of its own.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the Nirankaris opposed idol worship and Brahmin-led rituals. Statement 2: the movement did issue hukamnamas on correct practice and kept its own worship places and priests.

st.3: Spiritual nationalism rejected the idea of the nation as a mother goddess.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: spiritual nationalism saw the nation as a mother goddess. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Extremists carried nationalism beyond the educated elite to the masses.

st.3: Madan Lal Dhingra led India House after Krishnavarma left for Paris in 1907.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Savarkar led India House after Krishnavarma left; Dhingra was a member who shot Curzon Wyllie (1909). Statement 4 is incorrect: India House was founded by Shyamji Krishnavarma, not Har Dayal.

st.3: The Swarajists finally walked out of the legislatures in 1930.

x: All three statements are correct: the Responsivists (Lajpat Rai, Malaviya, Kelkar) wanted cooperation, C.R. Das died in June 1925, and the Swarajists finally left the legislatures in 1930 after the Lahore Congress call.

st.3: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was a leading Communist, not Forward Bloc, leader in Andhra.

x: All three statements are correct: Madduri Annapurnaiah was jailed for 18 months for 'Chicharapidugu', he led the Forward Bloc in Andhra with Peta Bapayya, and Sundarayya was a Communist leader.

st.3: The Simon Commission, appointed in November 1927, arrived in India on 3 February 1929.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Prakasam was APCC President 18 times. Statement 2 is incorrect: the fourth part of Naa Jeevita Yatra was written by Tenneti Viswanatham. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Simon Commission arrived on 3 February 1928.

st.3: It was issued by the Congress Working Committee.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the circular was issued by the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee, not the Working Committee. Statement 4 is incorrect: the APCC meeting at Machilipatnam was under Pattabhi Sitaramayya, not Prakasam.

st.2: Its Assembly was elected afresh in a general election held in 1953.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the first Andhra State had no Legislative Council (AP became bicameral in 1958). Statement 2: its Assembly was made up of the members elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952; there was no fresh election in 1953.

st.3: It rejected language as the main basis for reorganising provinces.

x: All three statements are correct: the Dhar Commission was appointed by the President of the Constituent Assembly, reported on 10 December 1948, and rejected language as the main basis, preferring administrative convenience.

st.2: He was an Arya Vysya whose ancestral village, Gajula Dinne, is in Nellore district.

x: All three statements are correct: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in Madras, was an Arya Vysya with Gajula Dinne (Nellore) as ancestral village, and spent about three years at Sabarmati.

st.4: It recommended retaining the Part A/B/C classification of states.
st.1: It was submitted on 30 September 1955 and made public on 1 November 1956.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Commission received about 1,52,250 memorandums. Statement 1 is incorrect: the report was made public on 9 October 1955 (1 November 1956 is when the reorganisation took effect). Statement 3 is incorrect: it recommended 16 states and 3 centrally administered territories. Statement 4 is incorrect: it recommended abolishing the Part A/B/C classification.

st.1: The views of the affected state legislature are not binding on Parliament.

x: All three statements are correct: the state's views are not binding on Parliament, no reference is needed for a Union Territory, and no fresh reference is needed for each amendment to the Bill.

st.1: The Levallois technique is a prepared-core flake technique of the Mesolithic.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the Levallois prepared-core flake technique belongs to the Middle Palaeolithic, not the Mesolithic. Statement 2: no Neanderthal fossil has been found in India.

st.4: All Satavahana inscriptions are in Sanskrit in the Brahmi script.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Myakadoni is in Ballari district, Karnataka, not Kurnool. Statement 4 is incorrect: Satavahana inscriptions are in Prakrit, not Sanskrit.

st.3: The Telugu word 'Vepuru' occurs in the Myakadoni inscription.

x: All three statements are correct: under the Salankayanas Sanskrit replaced Prakrit in most inscriptions, Kuntala Satakarni made Sanskrit the royal language, and 'Vepuru' occurs in the Myakadoni inscription (the Amaravati inscription has 'Nagabu').

st.1: In May 2025 the ASI decoded 11 Satavahana-era Prakrit-Brahmi inscriptions in the Nallamala forest of Nandyal district, Andhra Pradesh.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the 11 inscriptions decoded in May 2025 are in the Gundaram reserve forest, Peddapalli district, Telangana. Statement 2: the early Ikshvaku inscriptions are in Prakrit, not Sanskrit.

st.1: The reign of Santamula is called the golden age of Buddhism.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the golden age of Buddhism was under Virapurushadatta; Santamula performed Vedic sacrifices. Statement 2: the Ikshvaku kings were Vedic Hindus; Buddhism was patronised by their queens.

st.3: Its finds include an amphitheatre but no Vedic Ashvamedha altar.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Longhurst first excavated it in 1927. Statement 1 is incorrect: it was found in 1926 by A. Ranganatha Saraswati; R. Subrahmanyam dug it later. Statement 3 is incorrect: the finds include Santamula's Ashvamedha altar as well as the amphitheatre.

st.1: Caves 1-3 are Buddhist chaityas with stupas behind a pillared mandapa.
st.3: Navagraha figures appear on the kapota (eave) above the pillar capitals.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Cave 4 is the Durga cave with Ardhanarishvara on its back wall. Statement 1 is incorrect: Caves 1-3 have sanctums for the Trimurti (the caves are Brahmanical). Statement 3 is incorrect: the kapota carries Trimurti figures. Statement 4 is incorrect: there are five caves.

st.1: He is associated with building 108 Jain basadis.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Vijayaditya II is linked with the naming of Vijayawada. Statement 1 is incorrect: he is credited with 108 Shiva temples, not Jain basadis. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Kavirajamarga was composed by the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I.

st.3: Wheat was the only local grain.
st.4: He makes no mention of diamonds in the kingdom.
st.1: He criticised the queen's harsh and unjust rule.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: Marco Polo praised Rudramadevi's just rule. Statement 2: Motupalli merchants were not heavily taxed; the queen's abhaya grant lightened their dues. Statement 3: he said rice was the only grain. Statement 4: he described the diamond mines of the Golconda region.

st.3: The Kridabhiramamu of Vinukonda Vallabharaya, which describes the routes, depicts life in Rajahmundry.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Tripurantakam linked Motupalli to Ballari. Statement 2 is incorrect: Ketana's chief inland route ran from Kanchi through Nellore and Warangal to Ayodhya. Statement 3 is incorrect: Kridabhiramamu depicts life in Orugallu (Warangal).

st.1: Yusuf Adil Shah founded the Adil Shahi dynasty of Ahmadnagar, the first to break away from the Bahmanis (1489).

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Golconda broke away last (1518) and fell last (1687). Statement 1 is incorrect: the Adil Shahis ruled Bijapur; Ahmadnagar was the Nizam Shahis'. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Imad Shahis ruled from Ellichpur; Bidar was the Barid Shahi capital.

st.2: The People's War line helped the CPI sweep the 1945-46 elections.
st.1: In 1952 the communists won a majority of the 145 Andhra-region seats.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Prakasam's Andhra ministry fell on 15 November 1954. Statement 1 is incorrect: the communists won 41 of the 145 seats, not a majority. Statement 2 is incorrect: the People's War line cost the CPI heavily in 1945-46. Statement 4 is incorrect: in 1955 the CPI won only 15 of the 196 seats.

st.3: The Madras Government banned it.

x: All three statements are correct: the Kothapatnam summer school was held in 1937, taught politics and economics to young activists, and was banned by the Madras Government.

st.3: India has 57 PVTGs.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: India has 75 PVTGs. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Koya are a Scheduled Tribe but not a PVTG.

st.3: Keezhadi is a Sangam urban site on the Kaveri, contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation.
st.1: Arikamedu near Madurai was an Indo-Roman trading settlement.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Kaveripattinam (Puhar) had Yavana settlements. Statement 1 is incorrect: Arikamedu is near Puducherry. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Pugalur inscription records three generations of Chera rulers. Statement 3 is incorrect: Keezhadi lies on the Vaigai (Sivaganga district), not the Kaveri.

st.2: The Kudumiamalai inscription of the Pallava period is famous for music.

x: All three statements are correct: Mandagapattu claims a temple built without brick, timber, metal or mortar, the Kudumiamalai inscription is a music inscription, and it is credited to Mahendravarman I.

st.1: After Mahmud the Ghaznavids declined under Mongol pressure.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the Ghaznavids declined under Seljuk pressure; the Mongols came later. Statement 2 is incorrect: Yamini-ud-Daulah was conferred by the Abbasid caliph al-Qadir.

st.1: He entered India by the Gomal Pass.

x: All three statements are correct: Muhammad Ghori entered by the Gomal Pass, his first invasion (1175) was against Multan, and he took Lahore from Khusru Malik in 1186.

st.1: According to M.N. Srinivas, Sanskritisation brings positional change, not structural change, in the caste system.

x: All three statements are correct: Sanskritisation brings positional, not structural, change; 'Kshatriyaisation' is associated with Kulke; and Srinivas wrote 'The Remembered Village' and 'Social Change in Modern India'.

st.1: Language is not counted among the recognised bases of social stratification.

x: All three statements are correct: language is not a recognised basis of stratification, political power is a modern basis, and stratification ranks groups by unequal wealth, prestige and power.

st.3: Odisha has the largest ST population by number.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Bhil is the largest tribe and the Gond second. Statement 1 is incorrect: Lakshadweep has the highest ST share among States and UTs (Mizoram leads among States). Statement 3 is incorrect: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population by number.

st.1: The child is not to be kept at the police station at night for any reason.

x: All three statements are correct: the child cannot be detained at the police station at night, the trial is in camera with time limits for investigation and trial, and the NCPCR launched the POCSO e-Box in 2016.

st.2: Immunisation is delivered through the health system (NHM).

x: All three statements are correct: supplementary nutrition is given through the Anganwadi Centre, immunisation comes through the health system (NHM), and pre-school education is for children of 3-6 years.

st.2: Shyam Saran Negi of Kinnaur, Uttarakhand is known as independent India's first voter.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: about 12.4% of Andhra Pradesh's population was 60+ in 2021. Statement 2 is incorrect: Kinnaur is in Himachal Pradesh, not Uttarakhand. Statement 3 is incorrect: the India Ageing Report 2023 projects the elderly to outnumber children by 2046, not 2036.

st.1: When launched on 25 June 2015, it set the target of 'Housing for All' by 2022.

x: All three statements are correct: PMAY-U (25 June 2015) aimed at Housing for All by 2022, PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) targets 1 crore urban houses, and Rajiv Awas Yojana was subsumed into it in 2015.

st.3: A first offence is punishable with 6 months' to 2 years' imprisonment and a fine of ₹1,000-5,000.
st.1: They are non-cognizable and, except where the minimum term exceeds 3 months, triable summarily.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: a convict is disqualified under Section 8 of the RPA, 1951. Statement 1 is incorrect: PCR offences are cognizable. Statement 2 is incorrect: they are non-compoundable. Statement 3 is incorrect: a first offence carries 1-6 months and a fine of ₹100-500.

st.4: The National Helpline 14567 handles PoA and PCR grievances.
st.2: The State Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is headed by the Governor.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: relief ranges from ₹85,000 to ₹8.25 lakh under the 2016 Rules. Statement 1 is incorrect: the District committee is chaired by the District Magistrate. Statement 2 is incorrect: the State committee is headed by the Chief Minister. Statement 4 is incorrect: the PoA/PCR helpline is 14566 (14567 is the Elderline).

st.3: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993 is still in force.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan was the first chairman of the statutory NCM. Statement 2 is incorrect: Haj management moved to the Ministry of Minority Affairs only in 2016. Statement 3 is incorrect: the NCSK Act lapsed in 2004; the Commission now continues by resolution.

st.1: Dyscalculia is a specific learning disability related to writing.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the RPwD Act lists specific learning disabilities separately. Statement 1 is incorrect: dyscalculia relates to mathematics (writing is dysgraphia). Statement 3 is incorrect: under the 2017 definition the test is counting fingers at 3 metres, not 6.

st.2: The Information for All Programme is run by UNESCO.

x: All three statements are correct: UNESCO had 194 Member States, it runs the Information for All Programme, and Khaled El-Enany became its first Arab Director-General on 15 November 2025.

st.2: Of the two plans before it, that of Harry Dexter White of the USA was adopted.

x: All three statements are correct: the conference met in July 1944 at Bretton Woods with 44 nations, Harry Dexter White's plan won over Keynes's, and the ITO was never created, GATT filling the gap until the WTO.

st.2: The Trade Facilitation Agreement is the only new WTO agreement of its first 30 years.
st.1: Phytosanitary rules and technical standards are tariff barriers, not non-tariff barriers.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: phytosanitary rules and technical standards are non-tariff barriers. Statement 2: the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is the second new agreement besides the TFA. Statement 3: anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard inquiries are conducted by the DGTR, not the DGFT.

st.4: Its last Leaders' Summit was held at Colombo in 2017.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: India took over the chair for 2025-27 from Sri Lanka, not Bangladesh. Statement 4 is incorrect: the 2017 Leaders' Summit was at Jakarta.

st.3: India opted out of it in 2019.

x: All three statements are correct: RCEP was signed on 15 November 2020, covers about 30% of the world's population, and India opted out in November 2019.

st.2: Rafael Grossi of Brazil is the Director General of the IAEA.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Rafael Grossi is from Argentina, not Brazil. Statement 3 is incorrect: India's 2009 safeguards agreement covers only its civilian facilities.

st.1: Before it, the head of Fort William was styled the Governor-General of Bengal.
st.2: It kept the Presidencies of Bombay and Madras independent of Bengal.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Directors had to send revenue, civil and military letters to the British Government. Statement 1 is incorrect: before 1773 he was the Governor of Bengal; the Act created the Governor-General of Bengal. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act made Bombay and Madras subordinate to Bengal. Statement 4 is incorrect: it did not abolish the Court of Directors.

st.2: It provided Rs 10 lakh a year for education.
st.4: It barred Christian missionary activity in India.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the 1813 Act first asserted the Crown's sovereignty over the Company's territories. Statement 1 is incorrect: the monopoly ended except for tea and the China trade. Statement 2 is incorrect: it provided Rs 1 lakh a year. Statement 4 is incorrect: it permitted missionary activity.

st.4: It barred supplementary questions.
st.1: S.P. Sinha became the first Indian in the Viceroy's Executive Council, as Finance Member.
st.2: The additional members of the Central Legislative Council were raised to 60, a total of 69, with an elected majority.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: S.P. Sinha joined as Law Member. Statement 2: the 60 additional members kept an official majority at the Centre. Statement 3: bicameralism at the Centre came with the 1919 Act. Statement 4: the 1909 Act allowed supplementary questions.

st.3: It provided for a statutory commission after 10 years; the Simon Commission that followed had two Indian members.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the 1919 Act created the High Commissioner for India in London. Statement 2 is incorrect: the first Chancellor of the Chamber of Princes was the Maharaja of Bikaner. Statement 3 is incorrect: all seven members of the Simon Commission were British; it had no Indian.

st.1: The British monarch remained the nominal head of the new Dominions.

x: All three statements are correct: the monarch stayed the nominal head of the Dominions, the Governor-General acted on Dominion ministers' advice, and the Constituent Assembly was both sovereign constitution-maker and Dominion legislature.

st.2: Mahavira was the 23rd Tirthankara.
st.1: Parshvanatha was the first Tirthankara of Jainism.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Tripitaka are the Buddhist sacred texts. Statement 1 is incorrect: Rishabhanatha was the first Tirthankara (Parshvanatha was the 23rd). Statement 2 is incorrect: Mahavira was the 24th and last. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Adi Granth was compiled by Guru Arjan Dev.

st.1: 'Untouchability' is defined in Article 17 of the Constitution.
st.3: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act by an amendment of 1989.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Article 17 operates against private individuals too. Statement 1 is incorrect: 'untouchability' is not defined in the Constitution or the Act. Statement 3 is incorrect: the renaming came by the 1976 amendment (1989 is the SC/ST PoA Act). Statement 4 is incorrect: the Act keeps the year 1955 in its title.

st.3: The concept was borrowed from the United States.

x: All three statements are correct: PIL relaxes locus standi, S.P. Gupta (1981) is a key case, and the concept came from the USA.

st.1: The 4 per cent Muslim quota under the AP Act of 2007 was struck down by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in 2010.

x: All three statements are correct: the AP High Court struck down the 2007 quota in 2010 and the 2004 quota earlier, and in Sukhdev it held that caste alone cannot be the basis.

st.1: In Golaknath (1967), an 11-judge bench held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights and applied prospective overruling.
st.2: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) was heard by 11 judges.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Minerva Mills struck down Articles 368(4) and 368(5). Statement 1 is incorrect: Golaknath held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights. Statement 2 is incorrect: Kesavananda was heard by 13 judges, the largest bench. Statement 3 is incorrect: Minerva Mills was a five-judge bench.

st.1: The 102nd Amendment received assent on 11 August 2019.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the 102nd Amendment received assent on 11 August 2018. Statement 2: the 105th Amendment restored, not took away, the States' power to identify SEBCs.

st.1: It was passed as the 126th Amendment Bill, 2019.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: it was the 124th Amendment Bill, 2019. Statement 4 is incorrect: Janhit Abhiyan (2022) upheld it by 3:2.

st.1: If the two Houses disagree on a Constitutional Amendment Bill, there is no joint sitting and the Bill fails.

x: All three statements are correct: there is no joint sitting on an Amendment Bill, the Rajya Sabha can only recommend on a Money Bill within 14 days, and it can discuss the Budget but not vote on grants.

st.2: A resolution to remove the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha needs 14 days' notice.

x: All three statements are correct: impeachment is a quasi-judicial function needing one-fourth of the House to sign the notice, removal of the Deputy Chairman needs 14 days' notice, and the Rajya Sabha elects only its Deputy Chairman.

st.3: A member elected to a casual vacancy serves a full fresh six-year term.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the first retirements in 1952 were decided by lottery. Statement 1 is incorrect: the six-year term is fixed by the RPA, 1951, not the Constitution. Statement 3 is incorrect: a casual-vacancy member serves only the rest of the predecessor's term.

st.1: The salaries of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are voted annually by the Lok Sabha.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Speaker ranks with the Chief Justice, above Cabinet Ministers. Statement 1 is incorrect: their salaries are charged on the Consolidated Fund and not voted. Statement 2 is incorrect: a Governor holds office at the President's pleasure; there is no notice procedure.

st.2: In that review Nagaland's Assembly met for the fewest days and Odisha's for the most.

x: All three statements are correct: Assemblies met on average about 24 days, Nagaland met least (7) and Odisha most (43), and the 86th AIPOC was at Lucknow, the conference dating from 1921.

st.1: Their salaries are determined by Parliament and cannot be reduced after appointment except during a Financial Emergency under Article 360.

x: All three statements are correct: salaries can be cut only in a Financial Emergency (Art. 360), the oath is in the Third Schedule form, and a judge serves till 65 with the age question decided as Parliament provides.

st.3: The President is not a part of Parliament under the Constitution.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the President's supreme command of the Defence Forces is regulated by law. Statement 1 is incorrect: under Article 77 executive action is taken in the name of the President. Statement 3 is incorrect: under Article 79 the President is a part of Parliament.

st.4: A State that owes money to the Union can raise a fresh loan without the Union's consent.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Net Borrowing Ceiling rests on Article 293(3), not 292. Statement 4 is incorrect: such a State needs the Union's consent, which may carry conditions.

st.1: It was constituted in 1966.
st.2: Its first report dealt with Ethics in Governance.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the Second ARC was constituted in 2005 (1966 is the First ARC). Statement 2: its first report was on Right to Information (Ethics in Governance was the fourth). Statement 3: it did not recommend abolishing right to public services laws.

st.1: The 2006 amendment barred the NHRC from transferring complaints to the SHRC concerned.
st.4: The 2019 amendment raised the deemed members from four to five.
st.3: The 2019 amendment raised the human-rights expert members from two to three, with no requirement that one be a woman.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the 2006 amendment enabled the NHRC to transfer complaints to the SHRC. Statement 2: the term was cut to three years by the 2019 amendment, not 2006. Statement 3: one of the three expert members must be a woman. Statement 4: the deemed members rose from four to seven.

st.3: The recommending committee comprises the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.
st.4: It has a Chief Information Commissioner and up to 10 Information Commissioners appointed by the Prime Minister.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: removal for proved misbehaviour is by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry. Statement 1 is incorrect: the CJI is not on the committee. Statement 3 is incorrect: the committee has the Leader of Opposition, not the Speaker. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Commissioners are appointed by the President.

st.1: It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 4 August 2011 by V. Narayanasamy.

x: All three statements are correct: V. Narayanasamy introduced it on 4 August 2011, Singhvi's Standing Committee examined it, and the 2011 Bill became the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

st.2: The Central Council of Health was set up under Article 263 of the Constitution.

x: All three statements are correct: a council under Article 263 can investigate subjects of common interest, the Central Council of Health was set up under Article 263, and Sarkaria proposed Article 263 status for the renamed NDC.

st.1: The manner in which public acts and records are proved and their effect is decided by the State Legislatures by law.
st.3: The full faith and credit clause is modelled on the Constitution of Canada.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the manner of proof and effect is decided by Parliament by law. Statement 2: only final judgments of civil courts are executable anywhere in India. Statement 3: the clause is modelled on the US Constitution, not Canada's.

st.2: It ranked 8th overall and 5th among coastal States in the Export Preparedness Index 2022.

x: All three statements are correct: AP was a Top Achiever in BRAP 2020, ranked 8th overall and 5th among coastal States in EPI 2022, and won 5 National Panchayat Awards in 2025.

st.3: The Indrajit Gupta Committee's recommendation has not been adopted.

x: All three statements are correct: Germany, Sweden, Japan and Canada use State funding, full State funding bans private donations, and the Indrajit Gupta Committee's recommendation has not been adopted.

st.2: Its method was 'government aid with official supervision'.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Spencer Hatch ran the project under the YMCA in Travancore. Statement 1 is incorrect: its five-fold development was spiritual, mental, physical, economic and social, not political. Statement 2 is incorrect: its method was 'self-help with intimate expert counsel'.

st.1: Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not allocate plan funds to the States.

x: All three statements are correct: NITI Aayog has no fund-allocating role, it came into force on 1 January 2015 by a Cabinet resolution and is neither constitutional nor statutory, and it replaced Five-Year Plans with a 15-year Vision, 7-year Strategy and 3-year Action Agenda.

st.3: Bhogapuram airport is being developed by Adani on a DBFOT basis with a 40-year concession.
st.4: The AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2014 provides the PPP framework, including Swiss-challenge proposals.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Adani Ports acquired Krishnapatnam in 2020. Statement 2 is incorrect: Adani's acquisition of Gangavaram came in 2021, not 2019. Statement 3 is incorrect: Bhogapuram is being developed by GMR. Statement 4 is incorrect: the AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act is of 2001.

st.2: The Aadhaar Act was enacted in 2016.

x: All three statements are correct: Aadhaar proves identity, not citizenship; the Aadhaar Act was enacted in 2016; and it is a 12-digit biometric ID issued by UIDAI, set up in January 2009.

st.3: Tanks provide less than 3% of India's net irrigated area (2021-22).

x: All three statements are correct: groundwater meets about 64% of irrigation needs, India accounts for about 25% of global groundwater extraction, and tanks give under 3% (about 2.8%) of net irrigated area.

st.4: Global Hunger Index
st.2: Global Gender Gap Index

x: Only items 1 and 3 are UNDP measures: the Gender Empowerment Measure (1995) came before the Human Poverty Index (1997). Item 2 is not a UNDP measure: the Global Gender Gap Index is the WEF's. Item 4 is not a UNDP measure: the Global Hunger Index is published by Welthungerhilfe and Concern Worldwide.

st.3: NFHS-6 (2023-24) reported a TFR of 2.0 and a contraceptive prevalence rate of 69.1%.

x: All three statements are correct: UNFPA's 2021 'My Body is My Own' was the first UN report on bodily autonomy, MoHFW runs NFHS through IIPS Mumbai, and NFHS-6 reported a TFR of 2.0 and CPR of 69.1%.

st.1: India had 23 million-plus cities as per Census 1991.

x: All three statements are correct: there were 23 million-plus cities in 1991, and they held 42.6% of the urban population in 2011 and 37.8% in 2001.

st.1: SEWA pioneered bank linkage of SHGs in the mid-1980s.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: NABARD's SHG-Bank Linkage Programme is the world's largest microfinance programme. Statement 1 is incorrect: bank linkage was pioneered by MYRADA, not SEWA. Statement 3 is incorrect: savings-linked SHGs stood at about 143 lakh on 31 March 2025 (about 85 lakh was the 2017 level).

st.2: It replaced the Swarna Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana in 2013.
st.3: In Andhra Pradesh it is implemented by SERP (Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty).

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: DAY-NULM is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Statement 2: it replaced the Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SGSY was the rural scheme replaced by NRLM). Statement 3: in AP it is implemented by MEPMA; SERP handles the rural mission.

Only codes 2 and 4 are correct years: the National Social Assistance Programme dates from 1995 and the First National Health Policy from 1983. Code 1 is incorrect: the National Extension Service began in 1953, not 1950. Code 3 is incorrect: MGNREGA was enacted in 2005, not 1999.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh signed its urban-affairs MoU with UN-Habitat.

x: All three statements are correct: waste segregation reached about 96.07% in 2024-25, Anna Canteens with Rs 5 meals reopened in August 2024, and the urban-affairs MoU was with UN-Habitat.

st.1: It provides German (A1-B2) language training for overseas placement, mainly for IT professionals.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the German training is mainly for nurses, not IT professionals. Statement 2: the Letter of Intent was with FVCC of Japan, not a German body.

st.3: Land revenue and stamp duty are production taxes, not product taxes.

x: All three statements are correct: subsidies are added in moving from market prices to factor cost, excise duty and GST are product taxes, and land revenue and stamp duty are production (not product) taxes.

st.3: Critics point out that India's large GDP coexists with an HDI rank of about 130.

x: All three statements are correct: a labour-surplus economy has near-zero marginal productivity of surplus farm labour, capital formation needs adequate savings, and India's large GDP coexists with an HDI rank of about 130.

st.3: The pro-business reforms of the 1980s raised the MRTP asset limit to Rs 1,000 crore.
st.4: The 1991 reforms cut the industries reserved for the public sector from 17 to 4.
st.1: IFCI was set up in 1956, the year of the second Industrial Policy.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: IFCI was set up in 1948, the year of the first Industrial Policy. Statement 2: the IPR 1956 listed 17 industries in Schedule A and 12 in Schedule B. Statement 3: the 1980s reforms raised the MRTP limit to Rs 100 crore. Statement 4: the 1991 policy cut the reserved list from 17 to 8.

st.4: Inclusion is measured by GDP per capita alone.
st.2: In IDI 2018 India was 62nd of 74 emerging economies, and Norway topped them.
st.1: Its pillars are growth and development; inclusion; and governance and corruption.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the third pillar is intergenerational equity and sustainability. Statement 2: Lithuania topped the emerging economies in 2018; Norway topped the advanced economies. Statement 3: Lithuania topped in 2017, with Azerbaijan second. Statement 4: inclusion is measured by income, poverty and wealth indicators, not GDP per capita alone.

st.2: HDR 2025 was topped by Iceland, with South Sudan last.

x: All three statements are correct: HDR 2023-24 was topped by Switzerland (0.967), HDR 2025 by Iceland with South Sudan last, and in HDR 2021/22 Hong Kong (4th) ranked above Australia (5th).

st.3: The Rangarajan Expert Group put all-India poverty at 21.9%.
st.4: The Rangarajan urban poverty line was ₹972 per capita per month.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Tendulkar lines were ₹816 rural and ₹1,000 urban. Statement 2 is incorrect: under Tendulkar rural poverty (25.7%) was higher than urban (13.7%). Statement 3 is incorrect: Rangarajan put poverty at 29.5%; 21.9% is Tendulkar's. Statement 4 is incorrect: Rangarajan's urban line was ₹1,407 (₹972 was rural).

st.3: Wealth inequality is measured mainly from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).
st.1: Consumption inequality is measured mainly from the Census of India.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: consumption estimates may understate top incomes. Statement 1 is incorrect: consumption inequality comes from the NSS/HCES surveys of MoSPI, not the Census. Statement 3 is incorrect: wealth inequality comes from AIDIS. Statement 4 is incorrect: the top 10% median income was about 13 times the bottom 10%.

st.3: The Twelfth Plan targeted 4% manufacturing growth and 50 million new non-farm jobs.
st.2: The Twelfth Plan's third scenario was called 'Strong Inclusive Growth'.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Tenth Plan set monitorable targets for the Centre and each State. Statement 2 is incorrect: the third scenario was 'Policy Logjam'; 'Strong Inclusive Growth' was the first. Statement 3 is incorrect: the manufacturing target was 10% (4% was agriculture). Statement 4 is incorrect: the NDC lowered the 9% target to 8%.

st.3: Tax devolution to the States in Budget 2026-27 is ₹15,26,255 crore.

x: All three statements are correct: SASCI loans prevented pro-cyclical cuts in State capex, State capex rose from 2.17% to 2.37% of GDP, and devolution in Budget 2026-27 is ₹15,26,255 crore (total transfers ₹26,20,769 crore).

st.2: Under the RuPay-BHIM UPI incentive scheme, NPCI is the nodal agency.

x: All three statements are correct: zero MDR applies to RuPay debit and BHIM-UPI since 1 January 2020, NPCI is the nodal agency for the incentive scheme, and the 2026 Bill allows MDR on high-value UPI payments.

st.1: The total number of PMJDY accounts is about 14.72 crore.
st.3: About three-fourths of the accounts are in metro and urban areas.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: there are about 59.09 crore accounts (14.72 crore was the 2015 figure). Statement 2: women hold over half of the accounts. Statement 3: about three-fourths are in rural and semi-urban areas.

st.4: Credit creation is done by the RBI; commercial banks only distribute it.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: fiscal policy is made by the Ministry of Finance. Statement 4 is incorrect: credit creation is done by commercial banks; the RBI only controls it.

st.2: MUDRA (2015) provides development and refinance support for loans to large industries.
st.4: The Government and SBI are selling a combined 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to a private buyer.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: NHB was set up in 1988 under the NHB Act, 1987. Statement 2 is incorrect: MUDRA supports loans to micro units, not large industries. Statement 3 is incorrect: IFCI was set up in 1948 (1964 is IDBI). Statement 4 is incorrect: the 60.72% stake is being sold by the Government and LIC.

st.1: They can be set up anywhere in India and need not be located within a Special Economic Zone.

x: All three statements are correct: EOUs, EHTPs and STPs can be set up anywhere in India, they must export all their output, and EHTPs cover electronics hardware while STPs cover software.

st.1: The first KVK was set up in 1984 at Puducherry.
st.2: KVKs grew out of the recommendation of the Swaminathan Committee.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: KVKs are supervised through 11 ATARIs. Statement 1 is incorrect: the first KVK came up in 1974. Statement 2 is incorrect: KVKs grew out of the Mohan Singh Mehta Committee. Statement 3 is incorrect: KVKs are 100% funded by ICAR.

st.2: Crop Cultivator Rights Cards are issued under the AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 and are valid for five years.
st.4: The landowner's signature is not required to issue a CCRC.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the 2011 Act gave tenants Loan Eligibility Cards. Statement 2 is incorrect: a CCRC is valid for 11 months. Statement 3 is incorrect: a CCRC never transfers ownership. Statement 4 is incorrect: the landowner's signature is needed and is a major hurdle.

st.1: In 2010-11, small and marginal holdings were about 44% of all holdings but had about 85% of the operated area.
st.2: In 2015-16, small and marginal holdings were 86.2% of holdings with 74.3% of the area.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: semi-medium and medium holdings were 13.2% of holdings with 43.6% of the area. Statement 1 is incorrect: the figures are reversed; small and marginal holdings were about 85% of holdings with about 44% of the area. Statement 2 is incorrect: their share of area was 47.3%. Statement 4 is incorrect: Rajasthan ranked first by operated area (UP leads by number of holdings).

st.2: Existing private units in the mixed sector were allowed 25 years, after which their position was to be reviewed.
st.4: Foreign capital was barred from Indian industry.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the mixed sector had 6 industries. Statement 2 is incorrect: existing private units were given 10 years. Statement 3 is incorrect: the centrally regulated category had 18 industries. Statement 4 is incorrect: foreign capital was welcomed, with control in Indian hands.

st.1: BRAP was first released in 2015 by DIPP (now DPIIT) with NITI Aayog.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: in BRAP 2017 AP was 1st, Telangana 2nd and Haryana 3rd. Statement 1 is incorrect: the 2015 BRAP was released with the World Bank Group, not NITI Aayog. Statement 2 is incorrect: Gujarat topped BRAP 2015, with AP 2nd.

st.1: A Global Capability Centre is a third-party vendor doing outsourced work for many clients, not an in-house unit of a multinational.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: India has over 1,800 GCCs. Statement 1 is incorrect: a GCC is a multinational's own offshore unit doing its core work, not a third-party vendor. Statement 3 is incorrect: a PMI below 50 indicates contraction.

st.3: Visakhapatnam ranked first in per capita income in FY 2025-26, with the Southern Naval Command among its drivers.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Parvathipuram Manyam had the lowest GDDP, but the lowest per capita GDDP was Srikakulam's. Statement 3 is incorrect: Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command; the Southern Naval Command is at Kochi.

st.2: NMEO-OP (2021) aims to raise India's oil-palm area to 20 lakh ha.
st.3: NMEO-OP targets 28 lakh t of crude palm oil by 2025-26.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: AP's FFB output was 22.81 lakh MT in 2025-26. Statement 2 is incorrect: NMEO-OP aims at 10 lakh ha. Statement 3 is incorrect: its 2025-26 target is 11.20 lakh t of CPO (28 lakh t is the 2029-30 target). Statement 4 is incorrect: the import-dependence figures given are not right.

st.3: It targets 50% of all-India port cargo by 2047.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the target is 20% of all-India cargo by 2047. Statement 4 is incorrect: the AP Maritime Board is the nodal body for the non-major ports; Visakhapatnam, the major port, is under the Union.

st.2: In the primary market, transactions take place between the issuing company and investors.

x: All three statements are correct: the primary market deals in new securities and the secondary in existing ones, primary-market deals are between issuer and investor, and rights issues and private placements are primary-market transactions.

st.2: The 60°N parallel is not a great circle.

x: All three statements are correct: the Equator is the only parallel that is a great circle, so 60°N is not one, and the 0° and 180° meridians together form a great circle.

st.1: Its angular speed is 15° per minute.
st.2: Its linear speed is about 1,670 km/h at the Poles.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the angular speed is 15° per hour. Statement 2: the linear speed of about 1,670 km/h is at the Equator; it falls to zero at the Poles. Statement 3: linear speed varies with latitude.

st.4: The Glossopteris flora, cited in the continental-drift debate, is found only in the Laurasian continents.
st.2: Madagascar and Arabia were parts of Laurasia.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Greenland was part of Laurasia. Statement 2 is incorrect: Madagascar and Arabia were parts of Gondwanaland. Statement 3 is incorrect: Mesosaurus fossils are found in South America and southern Africa. Statement 4 is incorrect: Glossopteris is found across the Gondwana continents (India, Africa, South America, Australia, Antarctica), which is why it supports drift.

st.2: They were found by Colin Mackenzie in 1884.
st.1: They are the longest natural cave system in India.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Belum was declared a GSI Geo-Heritage Site in June 2025. Statement 1 is incorrect: Belum is the second-longest cave system in India, not the longest. Statement 2 is incorrect: it was found by Robert Bruce Foote in 1884. Statement 4 is incorrect: Belum is a karst cave in black limestone, not sandstone.

st.1: Namibia does not share a border with Zimbabwe.

x: All three statements are correct: Namibia and Zimbabwe do not share a border (they only come close at Kazungula), Luxembourg borders Belgium, Germany and France, and Indonesia borders Malaysia, Timor-Leste and Papua New Guinea.

st.1: Lake Erie is the only Great Lake wholly within the USA.
st.4: The Welland Canal connects Lakes Huron and Erie, bypassing Niagara Falls.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Straits of Mackinac link Lakes Michigan and Huron. Statement 1 is incorrect: Lake Michigan is the only Great Lake wholly in the USA. Statement 3 is incorrect: Lake Ontario is the easternmost; Superior is the westernmost. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Welland Canal links Lakes Erie and Ontario.

st.1: It is favoured by short summer nights, clear skies and calm, dry air.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: inversion causes fog, frost and smog and traps pollutants. Statement 1 is incorrect: inversion is favoured by long winter nights, not short summer nights. Statement 2 is incorrect: clear skies, not cloudy ones, favour inversion.

st.1: The Richter scale was devised by Charles Richter in 1955.
st.3: Category 1 on the Saffir-Simpson scale has wind speeds of 178–208 km/h.

st.3: The Amindivi group lies south of 10° N.

st.2: The Chambal Valley project is shared by Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
st.4: The Upper Bari Doab Canal draws water from the Beas.

st.4: APCNF natural farming depletes soil organic carbon.
st.3: Rainfed Area Development covers all 26 districts with Rs 30,000 per farm family.

st.1: Regulating deforestation, land-use zoning and control of industrial siting are response measures.

st.1: Rourkela Steel Plant, set up with Soviet collaboration, gets its ore from Keonjhar and Sundargarh.
